grading_policy.answer_first_policy: Identify the answer or claim first. Award credit for correct semantic equivalents and independently correct relevant reasoning even when a student uses different wording, notation, cases, examples, or a valid proof route. Use reasoning to verify the claim and detect material contradictions; do not require keyword matching.
grading_policy.element_credit_rule: Assign exactly one evidence level per scoring element. Do not duplicate points for repeated evidence. A material contradiction affects only its associated elements, not automatically every part of a multi-part answer.

questions.expected: For the context-free pumping lemma, |uz| <= p is not a required condition.

rubric.criterion: Selects d or an equivalent statement.

questions.expected: A stack alphabet is not part of the Turing-machine 7-tuple.

rubric.criterion: Selects b or an equivalent statement.

questions.expected: Unlike a DFA, a Turing machine has unbounded read/write tape and may move its head in both directions.

rubric.criterion: Selects b or an equivalent capability statement.

questions.expected: A language is decidable when some Turing machine decides it: it halts on every input and accepts or rejects.

rubric.criterion: Selects b or an equivalent always-halting-decider statement.

questions.expected: Assume L={a^n b^n c^n | n>=0} is context-free with pumping length p. Choose s=a^p b^p c^p, apply the CFL pumping decomposition s=uvxyz with |vxy|<=p and |vy|>0, observe the window meets at most two of the three blocks, and show every possible pumping location changes fewer than all three counts. Pumping with i=0 or i=2 produces a string outside L, contradicting the lemma.
questions.full_credit_rule: Full credit requires a valid CFL pumping-lemma contradiction: a correct witness, all relevant decomposition conditions, the two-block locality insight, a complete correct treatment of possible positions or an equivalent general argument, and a valid pumped-string contradiction. Equivalent rigorous pumping proofs receive credit.

material_errors.description: Treats the pumped window as able to span all three a/b/c blocks despite |vxy|<=p for the chosen witness.
Does not show that a permitted pump changes the required equal counts or otherwise leaves L.

scoring_elements.meaning: Assume L is context-free and obtain a pumping length p for a proof by contradiction.
Choose s=a^p b^p c^p and establish s is in L with length at least p.
Use a valid decomposition s=uvxyz and state/apply |vxy|<=p, |vy|>0, and pumping for all i>=0.
Explain that a substring of length at most p cannot touch all three p-length blocks, so the pumping window touches at most two regions.
Correctly cover the possible locations (within one block or crossing a/b or b/c), or give an equally rigorous general argument showing pumping cannot preserve all three equal counts.
Choose a permitted i such as 0 or 2, show the pumped string is not in L, and conclude the contradiction/non-context-freeness.

questions.expected: A configuration u q v represents current state q, tape contents uv, and a head scanning the first symbol of v. With tape 01101, state q3, and head on the second 1 (position 3), the configuration is 01 q3 101.
questions.full_credit_rule: Full credit requires the roles of u, q, and v, the head-at-first-symbol-of-v convention, and the correct concrete configuration 01 q3 101. Equivalent notation that unambiguously encodes the same tape/head/state receives credit.

material_errors.description: Places the head at the end of v or on the wrong symbol while claiming the standard u q v convention.

scoring_elements.meaning: Define u q v with q the current state and uv the tape contents (or an unambiguously equivalent configuration notation).
State that the head scans the first symbol of v, correctly locating the split in the tape contents.
For 01101 with q3 on position 3 (the second 1), give 01 q3 101 or an unambiguously equivalent notation.

questions.expected: For {a^n b^n c^n | n>=1}, reject input not of form a+ b+ c+. Return to the left end; repeatedly mark the leftmost unmarked a, then the leftmost unmarked b, then the leftmost unmarked c, returning left. When no unmarked a remains, accept only if no unmarked b or c remains; otherwise reject.
questions.full_credit_rule: Full credit requires an implementation-level mark-and-scan decider that rejects malformed input, marks one a/b/c per pass in the correct order, repeats, and verifies no unmatched b or c remains. Equivalent internal state names and marks receive credit.

material_errors.description: Marks symbols without ensuring one a, then one b, then one c in each pass, so equality is not checked.

scoring_elements.meaning: First verify the input is a nonempty a-block followed by b-block followed by c-block; reject malformed order or missing block.
In each pass, find and mark the leftmost unmarked a, then the leftmost unmarked b, then the leftmost unmarked c, with coherent scans/returns.
Repeat until no unmarked a remains and then explicitly check that no unmarked b or c remains.
Accept exactly when every required mark was paired; reject on a missing partner or leftover symbol.

questions.expected: The machine for {0^(2^n)} repeatedly sweeps left-to-right crossing off every other 0 until exactly one remains. On 0000 it starts in q1, a first pass leaves two 0s, returns left, a second pass leaves one 0, and accepts. The count halves 4->2->1; an odd count greater than 1 such as 000 is rejected.
questions.full_credit_rule: Full credit requires the repeated every-other-0 algorithm, a coherent trace for 0000 with the two halving passes and acceptance, plus the 4->2->1 explanation and the odd-count rejection behavior. Exact official state labels are not required when the trace is internally consistent.

material_errors.description: Claims an odd count greater than one such as 000 is accepted by the repeated-halving test.

scoring_elements.meaning: State the repeated left-to-right procedure that crosses off every other 0 until one remains.
Give a coherent start on 0000 and a first alternating-mark pass leaving two uncrossed 0s.
Return left, perform the second alternating pass leaving one 0, and accept.
Explain 4->2->1 and that an odd count greater than one (for example 000) is rejected.

questions.expected: A recognizer accepts members but may reject or loop forever on nonmembers. A decider accepts members, rejects nonmembers, and always halts. A recognizer-but-not-decider can search for a proof and accept when found while running forever otherwise. Every decidable language is recognizable, but not conversely.
questions.full_credit_rule: Full credit requires correct recognizer behavior, correct decider behavior, the halting contrast, a valid recognizer-not-decider example, and the decidable-implies-recognizable relationship. Equivalent examples and wording receive credit.

material_errors.description: Claims a recognizer must halt or reject every nonmember.
Claims a decider may loop forever on a nonmember.

scoring_elements.meaning: Members are accepted; a nonmember may be rejected or may cause nontermination.
A decider halts on every input, accepting exactly members and rejecting nonmembers.
Make explicit that recognition permits nontermination on no instances but decision does not.
Give a valid witness-search/proof-search or equivalent one-sided example.
State every decidable language is recognizable, but not conversely.

questions.expected: The three TM description levels are high-level algorithm, implementation-level tape mechanics, and formal 7-tuple. A palindrome example respectively compares outer symbols recursively/iteratively, marks/scans/compares outer symbols on tape, and specifies a 7-tuple with representative transitions.
questions.full_credit_rule: Full credit requires all three distinct levels and a correct palindrome construction/example for each. An exhaustive transition table is not required; a coherent 7-tuple-level sketch with representative transitions is sufficient.

scoring_elements.meaning: Identify a high-level algorithm and give a correct palindrome strategy such as repeatedly comparing outer symbols.
Identify tape mechanics and explain a coherent mark-scan-compare-move-inward palindrome procedure.
Identify the formal 7-tuple level and give states, alphabets, or representative transitions sufficient to show the construction.
